response.message:
I've drawn an IBM Cloud flow for this. Synthetic sensor data enters through Event Streams and maintenance records land in Cloud Object Storage. From there, features are built, a model is trained and checked on a later held-out time period, and versioned in watsonx.ai. A batch job scores equipment, Watson OpenScale watches for drift, and a small Code Engine app writes a work-order draft that an operator must approve. Nothing controls equipment automatically. None of these services, the region or account access has been checked or deployed.

**First local test:** run the synthetic data through the flow with a scripted (mocked) model. That shows records connect, versions are tracked, drift checks fire and drafts are created correctly, but it says nothing about how well the model predicts. Real model checking means training on the synthetic history and scoring it on a later time window it hasn't seen.

How many days before a failure should a warning reach the operator, for example 7 or 30 days?

proposal.title: IBM Cloud predictive maintenance end-to-end sketch
proposal.body: Scope: synthetic sensor histories and maintenance records → ingestion → features → time-split training/evaluation → versioned model → batch scoring → drift monitoring → operator-approved work-order draft. Assumptions: region not selected, IBM plans/model access unverified, no automatic equipment control. Design intent only; no native IBM generator for these ML components yet, so engineering is required.

response.message: Here's what's working: the emulation found no failing checks. The design is complete and connected, and it still meets your rules: drafts only, operator approval, and no control of equipment. The first blocker is not a design mistake. Our generator has no native IBM implementation yet for Event Streams ingestion, Spark feature preparation, watsonx.ai training, the model registry or batch scoring. The two synthetic sources also need a plan for how they are referenced or imported. The only supported IBM contract is private Object Storage. If I used it, we would shrink this application down to storage, so I've left the board unchanged. Fixing these blockers is product engineering work: we need native IBM generators for each block. A reproducer exists: design revision 2, artifact 494d3286…, 8 resource-block gaps. Even after those are built, a pass with a scripted model only proves the wiring. Real model quality needs a later held-out time window. One decision would let us start the data-source plan: should the synthetic sensor histories and maintenance records be generated as files dropped into Object Storage, or streamed live into Event Streams for the test?
